chunks.arabic_text: وَ سَأَلَ إِسْحَاقُ بْنُ يَزِيدَ أَبَا جَعْفَرٍ عَلَيْهِ السَّلَامُ: عَنِ الرَّجُلِ يَدْخُلُ مَكَّةَ فَيَقْطَعُ مِنْ شَجَرِهَا فَقَالَ

translations.en: Isḥāq ibn Yazīd asked Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام about a man who enters Makkah and cuts from its trees, so he said:

chunks.arabic_text: «اِقْطَعْ مَا كَانَ دَاخِلًا عَلَيْكَ وَ لَا تَقْطَعْ مَا لَمْ يَدْخُلْ مَنْزِلَكَ عَلَيْكَ».

translations.en: "Cut what has entered upon you, and do not cut what has not entered into your dwelling upon you."

en.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling about cutting the trees of Makkah. It permits cutting what has extended into a person's own space while forbidding cutting what remains outside and has not entered one's dwelling.
en.seo_question: Is it permissible to cut tree branches in Makkah if they extend into your dwelling?

key_terms.مَكَّةَ: Makkah, the sacred sanctuary in which special rulings apply
key_terms.شَجَرِهَا: its trees, referring to the trees of Makkah
key_terms.اِقْطَعْ: cut; an imperative permitting cutting in the stated case
key_terms.دَاخِلًا: entering or encroaching into one's space
